body: Multibaggers combine earnings growth with a rising multiple (Mayer, Phelps, Motilal). Start at a low multiple so both engines can work. Radico ≈ 7.5 × 5. NVIDIA post-2023 was earnings-only (multiple fell).
title: Twin engine: EPS growth × P/E rerating

body: Cases: Microsoft (Nadella 2014, $36 -> ~15x), AMD (Su 2014, ~$1.6 -> ~140x), Domino's (Doyle 2010, ~13x under him), Enphase (Kothandaraman 2017, ~400x then -90%), Meta (founder self-reset 2022-23, ~9x), Apple (Jobs 1997, then 2003-12 ~110x). Common pattern: (1) the stock is priced as a declining or dying business — P/E 9-15x or P/S <1x, often near-bankrupt; (2) the new leader publicly kills a sacred cow (Windows-first, low-margin segments, the old recipe, metaverse spending) and names a few measurable targets; (3) a single verifiable proof point appears early — Azure >100% growth, Zen benchmark demos, a +14% same-store-sales quarter, quarter-after-quarter gross-margin gains, an opex cut with a buyback; (4) returns come first from survival/rerating, then from EPS. Failure modes: Enphase shows a real operational turnaround can be overwhelmed by policy/cycle; turnaround investors should still ask whether demand is structural. Process rule for memory: don't buy the announcement; buy (or size up) after the first proof print, when the price usually still reflects the old narrative. Expected drawdowns even after the turn: -35% to -67% (MSFT 2022, AMD 2022).

data.signal: first measurable proof point after a public strategy reset

title: Turnarounds under a new CEO: the first proof print is the signal

body: Primary NSE Indices data (TR = total return; base 1 Apr 2005). Nifty200 Momentum 30 (whitepaper data to 27 Feb 2026): 19.19% CAGR since inception vs 15.08% for Nifty 200, at higher volatility; maximum drawdowns of momentum indices 68% (Nifty200 Mom 30), 73% (Midcap150 Mom 50), 70% (Nifty500 Mom 50) vs 64%, 73%, 64% for parents - 'momentum strategies ... thrive in trending markets but face challenges during market reversals.' Factsheets as of 30 Oct 2026: Nifty200 Momentum 30 TR 18.05% since 2005 but 7.93% over 5 years and -8.48% over 1 year (vol 22.3% since inception); Nifty200 Quality 30 TR 16.58% since 2005 (5y 6.96%, 1y -8.86%; vol 17.9%, beta 0.79 vs Nifty 50); Nifty500 Value 50 TR 10.28% since 2005, 5y -1.93%, 1y -19.56% (vol 27.2%); Nifty 50 TR 12.15% since Nov-1995 (5y 6.70%, 1y -9.45%, YTD-2026 -10.91%; P/E 19.3). Nifty500 Multifactor MQVLv 50 (momentum+quality+value+low-vol, data to 31 Dec 2024): 21.11% CAGR since 2005 vs 14.97% for Nifty 500 TR, at lower volatility (17.4% vs 20.6%); positive in 100% of rolling 5-year windows but negative in 15.5% of 1-year windows (worst -48.6%). Lessons: quality/low-vol give most of the premium with smaller drawdowns; momentum and value are cyclical (2026 drawdown hit both); all are back-tested from 2005 for indices launched 2018-2024 (look-ahead/selection bias in launch timing). Actionable: a quality/low-vol core is a reasonable passive baseline to beat before claiming stock-picking skill.
title: NSE factor indices (2005-2026): momentum, quality and multifactor beat the cap-weighted market, with deep drawdowns in momentum and value
